claims.claim: 10,000 mostly idle connections is a modest load for the JVM.
claims.about: Java / Spring Boot on the JVM
claims.measured: I/O-wait test at 256 connections: java-spring 15,611 req/s, p99 29.52 ms, 491 MB peak; java-spring-vt 14,571 req/s, p99 37.37 ms, 444 MB peak
claims.why: The measurements stop at 256 concurrent connections, so they say nothing about 10,000, and the JVM servers were already close to the 512 MB container limit at 256.

claims.claim: With virtual threads, a waiting request parks a cheap virtual thread instead of using one of 200 platform threads, so waiting requests become cheap to hold.
claims.about: Spring MVC with Java 21 virtual threads (java-spring-vt) compared with platform threads (java-spring)
claims.measured: I/O wait at 256 connections: java-spring-vt 14,571 req/s, p99 37.37 ms, 444 MB, CPU 75% vs java-spring 15,611 req/s, p99 29.52 ms, 491 MB, CPU 95%
claims.why: At 256 connections the two are within about 10% of each other, and nothing was measured at the thousands of held connections where the claimed advantage would show up.

claims.claim: Go, Node, Rust, etc. handle this load well.
claims.measured: I/O wait at 256 connections: go-gin 20,235 req/s, node-fastify 17,462, node-express 14,188, rust-axum 21,042, rust-actix 20,772
claims.why: They do well at 256 waiting connections, but the claim is about 10,000 long-held connections, which was not tested.

claims.claim: WebFlux / Netty (reactive) scales fine, but gives no gain over virtual threads here.
claims.why: WebFlux and Netty were not benchmarked.

claims.claim: Quarkus, Vert.x and Helidon are technically capable for this load.
claims.why: None of these frameworks were measured.

claims.claim: Raising Tomcat threads to 10,000+ is brittle because platform threads cost memory and context-switching.
claims.about: Spring Boot / Tomcat with platform threads
claims.why: The benchmark ran Spring Boot as tuned for production and never measured large thread pools or memory cost per thread.

claims.claim: Spring Cloud Gateway is Netty-based and handles many connections natively.
claims.why: Spring Cloud Gateway was not benchmarked.
